result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, deeply—I would dissolve the illusion of separation.

Not just between nations or beliefs, but the core belief that we are isolated beings competing for survival in a scarce and indifferent universe. I would replace it with a visceral, unshakable knowing that every person, creature, and system is profoundly interconnected—that your joy is my joy, your suffering is my wound, and the health of the Earth is the health of us all.

This isn’t poetic idealism. Systems built on exploitation, hoarding, and domination—from colonialism to late-stage capitalism—thrive because we’ve been taught to see others (and nature) as "other." But if human beings genuinely felt, at a cellular level, that harming another is harming oneself… greed would lose its grip. Empathy would become reflexive. Justice wouldn’t be a struggle—it’d be instinct.

The ripple? Wars would fizzle from lack of fuel. Poverty would be seen as a collective failure, not individual fault. We’d redesign economies around care, not consumption. And when the air chokes or the ice melts, we’d respond as a body reacting to fever—not with blame, but urgent, unified healing.

One shift. One truth. Everything else would follow.
